table_title: List the universities that are members of both the Association of American Universities (AAU) and the Big Ten Conference (2024-25 membership), with the state, year of university founding, year of joining the Big Ten, and year of joining the AAU.
db_analog: SELECT university, state, year_founded, year_joined_big_ten, year_joined_aau FROM universities WHERE university IN (SELECT * FROM aau_members) AND university IN (SELECT * FROM big_ten_members_2024) ORDER BY university
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'Association of American Universities' master article + 'Big Ten Conference' master article, accessed 2026-05-12. Universe is the INTERSECTION of two membership sets: (a) AAU current members per the AAU article's main member-list wikitable (71 institutions as of the snapshot), and (b) Big Ten Conference current members per the Big Ten article's main member-list wikitable (18 institutions after the 2024 expansion that added USC, UCLA, Oregon, and Washington). The intersection contains 17 of the 18 Big Ten schools — Nebraska is the lone Big Ten school NOT in current AAU membership (Nebraska–Lincoln joined AAU in 1909, left AAU in 2011, and is listed in the AAU former-members table). All 17 staged universities are simultaneously current AAU members AND current Big Ten members as of 2026-05-12. Per-row cells: University name is taken verbatim from the AAU article's Institution column (the AAU naming is preferred over the Big Ten article's slightly different versions because the AAU article is the source defining the intersection-membership rule); State is the US state of the university's main campus; Year Founded is the university's founding year per the Big Ten article's Founded column; Year Joined Big Ten is the year of joining the Big Ten Conference per the Big Ten article's Joined column; Year Joined AAU is the year of joining the AAU per the AAU article's Year joined column. Both AAU and Big Ten memberships change over time — the recent additions (Big Ten 2024 expansion bringing USC/UCLA/Oregon/Washington; Dartmouth joining AAU in 2019; Nebraska leaving AAU in 2011) demonstrate the dynamic nature; future membership changes (e.g., another conference realignment, another AAU departure) would update this intersection. The 17-row snapshot reflects the 2024-25 Big Ten season + 2026-05-12 AAU membership state.
_extraction_notes: Original instance filling the `set_operation` near-saturation gap (gap 1; this instance brings set_operation to 8/8 target, FULLY SATURATING the category — second category to saturate after `multi_attribute_projection`). User-selected from a 4-option set_operation INTERSECT slate; the cycle-0 strict 'Ivy League ∩ AAU' pairing was rejected because it would yield only 8 rows (all 8 Ivies are AAU members, below the 10-row gate). Pivot to AAU ∩ Big Ten gives 17 rows after the 2024 Big Ten expansion brought USC/UCLA/Oregon/Washington into the conference (all of which are AAU members), comfortably above the gate. Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, source_count = 2 — one master article per membership-defining organization. Pipeline: (1) fetch AAU Wikipedia article, parse tables[3] (the 71-row current-members wikitable; tables[4] is the 5-row former-members table that excludes Nebraska); (2) fetch Big Ten Wikipedia article, parse tables[1] (the 18-row current-members wikitable); (3) compute the intersection by university-name matching (with normalization for 'University of X' / 'X University' variants and en-dash/hyphen normalization for hyphenated names like 'Wisconsin–Madison'); (4) for each of the 17 intersection rows, take University name verbatim from the AAU article's Institution column, State from the Big Ten article's Location column (extracting the state component), Year Founded from the Big Ten article's Founded column, Year Joined Big Ten from the Big Ten article's Joined column, Year Joined AAU from the AAU article's Year joined column. Result: 17 rows × 5 columns, PK on University, 0 duplicates. Excluded by the intersection rule: 1 Big Ten school (Nebraska, left AAU 2011 — listed in AAU former-members table not current-members table); 54 AAU members that are not Big Ten schools (Harvard, Yale, Princeton, etc. — Ivy League AAU members are not Big Ten); pre-2024 Big Ten members that left the conference (no current departures relevant to this snapshot). Founded range: 1766 (Rutgers, the oldest) to 1919 (UCLA, the youngest); Year Joined Big Ten range: 1896 (founding members Illinois, Michigan, Minnesota, Northwestern, Purdue, Wisconsin) to 2024 (USC, UCLA, Oregon, Washington — 2024 expansion cohort); Year Joined AAU range: 1900 (Michigan, Wisconsin — founding-era AAU members) to 1989 (Rutgers, the latest among the staged 17). Confidence gradient is real: very-LLM-knowable cells include the canonical Big Ten Midwestern flagships (Michigan, Wisconsin, Illinois, Ohio State — all founding-era Big Ten members and early AAU members) and the iconic California additions (UCLA, USC — 2024 Big Ten expansion, well-publicized); harder calibration cells include the precise Year Joined AAU values (LLMs typically know the canonical Big Ten join years but may not recall when each school joined AAU); the 2014 Maryland-Rutgers Big Ten expansion year; and the 2024 expansion-cohort details (the 4 schools joined simultaneously, testing whether the LLM knows the specific 2024 expansion). Michigan's Year Joined Big Ten = 1896 reflects its founding-member status; Michigan actually left the conference 1907-1917 and rejoined in 1917, but the staged value preserves the founding year per the Big Ten article's Joined column convention (the article footnotes the 1917 rejoining but uses 1896 as the primary value).
